items.comparator: The article says yield improved from 72% to nearly 90%; no other baseline or control is described.

items.signal: Reported yield improvement in a specialty-chemicals project using an AI system and autonomous lab. Potentially distinctive execution capability, but the article does not identify the customer, process, or independent validation.

items.comparator: Company co-founder’s comparison: delivery in some cases took two months versus a typical 12 to 18 months; the source does not detail the comparison set.
items.quantitative_outcome: The article reports that the company’s approach has “in some cases, cut delivery times to two months from the typical 12 to 18.”
items.signal: Reported delivery-time reduction attributed to a proprietary AI platform and a network of more than 500 partner factories. The source does not isolate AI’s contribution from the manufacturing network or provide case-level evidence.

items.company: Pathos AI / Tempus AI / Bristol Myers Squibb
items.quantitative_outcome: none stated; the reported move is a five-year, $55 million data-licensing agreement for a longitudinal dataset drawn from hundreds of thousands of neurological-disease patients, plus a three-year exclusivity window for BMS to use Pathos Foundry in neuroscience.
items.signal: Distinctive access to a large longitudinal neurological-patient dataset, paired with AI analysis and time-limited BMS exclusivity, could become a hard-to-copy data advantage. No measured operating benefit is reported.

items.quantitative_outcome: none stated; the companies announced plans for a 100 million-cell dataset combining more than 11,000 proteomic secretome profiles across more than 150,000 immune-cell perturbation conditions.
items.signal: The planned multimodal immune dataset, with foundational commitments from GSK, Pfizer, Sanofi, Graph Therapeutics, and Turbine, is a distinctive data-access move with potential future value for AI-driven research. No measured operating benefit is reported; the dataset is planned, not an achieved outcome.
items.source: Business Wire press release carried by Ritzau

items.quantitative_outcome: Insilico reported: “during the first ten months of this year, we identified 11 developmental candidates for our internal pipelines”; it also said the total number nominated since 2021 reached 35. The report says target nominations were completed for two collaboration programmes and a milestone was reached for the first programme.
items.signal: Candidate output and completion of a predefined discovery milestone are measurable activity/capability signals, but the report gives no baseline or comparative measure demonstrating an operating benefit attributable to AI.

items.comparator: No baseline or comparison period stated; the report says processing turnaround times were reduced by over 70%.
items.quantitative_outcome: “AI-enabled workflows reduced trade-document processing turnaround times by over 70%.” The same report says new-to-bank business-banking onboarding volumes grew by over 80%, supported partly by AI-enabled workflows.
items.signal: AI-enabled trade-document workflows with a reported processing-time reduction; the report does not provide the measurement method or establish how much of the onboarding growth was attributable to AI.

items.comparator: No baseline or comparison period stated; the reported reduction is in time underwriters spend processing complex life-insurance cases.
items.quantitative_outcome: “reduced the time underwriters spend processing complex life insurance cases by 59%.”
items.signal: An AI underwriting copilot is reported to reduce processing time for complex cases, a workflow benefit that may be harder to replicate without comparable underwriting data and workflow integration. items.comparator: No baseline or comparison period stated for the 82% share; the company reported total customer-service volume as the denominator.
items.quantitative_outcome: “AI service representatives handled about 1,484 million customer service interactions in the first nine months of 2026, or 82% of its total service volume.” The report also says AI resolved 91% of requests end to end.
items.signal: Large-scale AI handling of service interactions and end-to-end resolution could reflect an advantage built on operational scale and accumulated service data. The figures are company-reported and unaudited; the source notes that counting methods and later human escalation are not specified.

items.comparator: No before-and-after comparator; the announcement describes data coverage rather than a measured operating improvement.

items.signal: Partnership to embed Hamilton Lane’s proprietary fund- and deal-level data in FactSet’s portfolio analytics platform. This is a distinctive data-access move that could become an advantage; the announcement reports no measured workflow, cost, or investment outcome.

items.quantitative_outcome: A customer reported that Reach detected security-control changes within five minutes of deployment, investigated them in under ten minutes, and remediated or approved them in under an hour. TAG Infosphere’s independent ROI analysis reported more than 160 hours saved per week and a 156% return. The release does not state a comparison baseline for the customer timings or ROI figures.
items.signal: AI-driven security-control analysis and remediation is associated with reported response times and labor savings; potentially distinctive operational benefit, but the evidence is reported by the company and does not establish a competitor comparison.
items.source: Reach Security announcement distributed by GlobeNewswire; it attributes the customer timings to one customer and the ROI figures to TAG Infosphere.

items.quantitative_outcome: “delivering audit-ready verdicts in 99 seconds on average.” The source gives no comparator or baseline.
items.signal: An average time-to-verdict claim for agentic SOC investigation; a workflow-speed signal, though no comparative evaluation or customer-specific measurement is given.
items.source: Sekoia announcement distributed by GlobeNewswire. The 99-second claim appears in the release’s product description; the separate Frost & Sullivan recognition is not itself a measured operating outcome.

items.quantitative_outcome: No measured operating-benefit outcome stated in the article. The company released an open benchmark for evaluating AI models on third-party risk management and attack resistance; the benchmark uses baselines and confidence intervals, but the article does not report a specific result for SecurityScorecard or a model.
items.signal: A distinctive benchmark and evaluation framework could build influence or data access in AI security testing, but the reported event supplies no measured advantage for the company itself. Weak candidate; included as a data/benchmark move, not as demonstrated operating benefit.

items.quantitative_outcome: “Tools connected to AIX are resolved 30% faster, with fewer escalations, than unconnected tools in the same fab.” The same article reports the company said a model forecasts electrostatic chuck failures 30 days in advance with “more than 90% accuracy.”
items.signal: AI platform connected to more than 37,000 process chambers in customer fabs, with reported service-resolution and predictive-maintenance results. The connected-versus-unconnected comparison within the same fab is a potentially relevant operating benchmark; durable advantage is not established by this report alone.
items.source: Industrial AI News, reporting remarks at Applied Materials’ SEMICON West technology breakfast; includes a Micron customer comment, but the cited numerical comparisons are attributed to the company.
